author: blu
body: An index over RFC 7932's 13504 dictionary words, so a position in the input can ask "is there a dictionary word here" without comparing itself against all of them. The corpus itself is BrotliDict, which is generated; this is the part that is written rather than extracted, so it lives in its own chapter.

author: blu
body: The corpus is carried inside the index for the same reason -- one load, threaded -- because every reference to a list constant rebuilds it and the corpus is a megabyte.

author: blu
body: Four is also the shortest word the corpus has, so this floor now excludes nothing. It is a floor on the SEARCH, not a judgement about any stream: the plan as a whole is still costed against not using the dictionary, which is what makes a marginal word safe to take.

author: blu
body: The hash is over the four bytes a word starts with, which is also the shortest word in the corpus, so every word can be indexed by it.

author: blu
body: An index with no slots. Every lookup answers minus one, so a caller that does not want the dictionary -- input too short to repay a megabyte of tables -- takes the same path as one that looked and found nothing.

author: blu
body: The walk keeps the LONGEST word that matches, not the first. A shorter candidate is rejected on its length before its bytes are touched, so the common case costs one comparison of two integers.

author: blu
body: Answers a SLOT, not a word. The caller needs the length and the index within that length to build a distance, and both come off the slot.

author: blu
body: The index within its own length, which is the word id transform zero uses. Slots are numbered in corpus order, so subtracting the length's own base offset and dividing by the length recovers it without a table.

author: blu
body: So a candidate is scored rather than measured: eight bits earned per byte consumed, less the width of the word id it needs. That is an estimate and it is meant to be -- the PLAN is still costed exactly, against the same plan without transforms, so a bad estimate costs ratio and can never cost correctness.

author: blu
body: Every usable transform tried against one candidate word, cheapest test first: a length that cannot win is rejected before a byte is read.

author: blu
body: The plain lookup in the same packed form, so a caller can ask for the dictionary WITHOUT transforms and get an answer of the same shape. Transform zero is the identity, so this is that answer.
